summary: The core is built as a scan-time hardware pipeline. A 634x525 raster counter at the board's 20 MHz pixel rate drives tile fetches. A per-scanline sprite machine fills ping-pong line buffers, and a staging-RAM copy into the sprite RAM happens during two lines after the visible area. On the SSIO sound board, MAME precomputes a volume table, but the core instead implements the actual divider chain (E11/D11/C12), the 82S123 PROM, a 74166-style shift-register clock and per-channel down-counters that gate the AY outputs. Nothing in the code follows MAME's tilemap callbacks, its per-frame sprite loop or its handler decomposition.

findings.note: A single hcnt/vcnt scanner (634 clocks x 525 lines with a top_frame interlace toggle) is the timebase for video fetch, sprite processing, buffer swap and CTC triggers. MAME has no such scanner.

findings.signal: per-line sprite machine into ping-pong line buffers
findings.note: On every line, a phase counter steps through all 128 sprites, compares the upper bits of an adder (sp_vcnt(8:5)=F) for a Y hit, and writes nonzero 4-bit pixels into two 256x16 line buffers selected by a V bit. MAME instead loops over the whole frame, from the last sprite down, with a priority bitmap and 'draw once' marking.

findings.signal: adder-based Y compare, not MAME's formula
findings.note: The core computes sp_vcnt = vflip + (vpos<<1) - 1 and tests the high bits, the way an adder plus gate would. MAME computes sy=(241-vpos)*2 and clamps.

findings.signal: sprite staging RAM copied during vblank lines
findings.note: The CPU writes to a cache RAM, and a transfer counter (vcnt(0)&hcnt(8:1)) copies it into the active sprite RAM on lines 500-501. MAME does not model this double buffering.

findings.signal: tile fetch phased on H counter bits
findings.note: The video RAM address is built from vflip(8:4)&hflip(8:4)&hcnt(1). Code and attribute are latched at hcnt(3:1)=6/7, and the pixel is selected by hflip(2:1) XOR the flip bit from two separate 2-bit-plane ROMs. MAME uses a tilemap callback.

findings.signal: sprite/background priority as a mux on low pixel bits
findings.note: The palette address is a combinational mux that shows the background when sprite bits (2:0)=000. MAME gets the same result in software through pri[] marking and an 'if (pix & 0x07)' test.
trg2 is a level over the vblank line range and trg3 fires at line 493 of the top field. MAME pulses trg2/trg3 at scanlines 0/240 in a timer callback.

findings.signal: SSIO divider chain named by chip location
findings.note: div_E11 (74161 bits), div_D11 (decade) and div_C12 (7-bit ripple) count from a 4 MHz enable, a read of 0xE000 clears them, and the IRQ comes from div_C12(6). MAME uses a periodic interrupt callback instead.

findings.signal: PROM-driven duty-cycle modulation as gates and counters
findings.note: The 82S123 PROM is addressed by divider bits, and a serialized bit acts as a clock that decrements per-channel 4-bit counters loaded from AY ports, which gate each AY channel. MAME precomputes a gain table from the PROM and calls set_output_gain.

findings.signal: AY bus control as pin-level gates
findings.note: BDIR/BC1 are derived as NOR-style gate expressions of the chip select and A0/A1, and the chips are instantiated with pin-level ports (A8, A9_L, BC2).
The CPU and SSIO address decode match MAME's maps, as any correct core must.
Interleaving CPU and video RAM access is ordinary FPGA resource engineering.
